reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n, under the hypothesis 3 ≤ n, and then for every real number κ, under the hypothesis 4 ≤ κ, make the following definitions in the displayed order.

Let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), the real n-dimensional Euclidean space with coordinates indexed by Fin n = {0,…,n−1}, its standard ℓ² norm, Borel structure, and Euclidean Lebesgue measure volume. Let G = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, the full real orthogonal group O(n), including both determinant signs, with its matrix Borel structure. Write O also for the underlying real n-by-n matrix of an element O ∈ G. Let μ be the canonical Haar measure normalized on the whole compact group G; thus μ is the full-group Haar probability measure.

Define
  νpos = 2 · (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det O = 1}),
  νneg = 2 · (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det O = −1}),
where the multiplier 2 is an extended nonnegative real scalar acting on measures. For use in the following definitions, abbreviate the real matrix expression
  A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
Define γ : G → Measure(E) by letting γ(O) be multivariateGaussian with mean 0 ∈ E and matrix parameter A(O)⁻¹. Precisely, the multivariateGaussian convention is the pushforward of canonical standard Gaussian measure on E under z ↦ 0 + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM(CFC.sqrt(A(O)⁻¹))(z). The matrix inverse is the standard totalized matrix inverse; the covariance interpretation of this Gaussian convention is the one valid for positive semidefinite matrix parameters.

For O ∈ G and x ∈ E, with v = WithLp.ofLp(x) its coordinate vector, define
  p(O,x) = [√(det A(O)) / (2π)^(n/2)] · exp(−(v · (A(O)v))/2).
In the denominator, n is coerced to a real number and (2π)^(n/2) is a real power, with real division by 2, not a power with a natural-number exponent. The products O + Oᵀ, A(O)v, and v · (A(O)v) are respectively matrix addition, matrix-vector multiplication, and the coordinate dot product. Define the real functions on E
  qpos(x) = ∫_G p(O,x) dνpos(O),
  qneg(x) = ∫_G p(O,x) dνneg(O).
Then define
  Ppos = νpos.bind γ,
  Pneg = νneg.bind γ,
namely the measures obtained by integrating the displayed measure kernel γ against νpos and νneg, respectively.

Define the real numbers
  δ = sup {z ∈ ℝ : there exists a measurable set B ⊆ E such that z = |(Ppos(B)).toReal − (Pneg(B)).toReal|},
  a = ∫_E √(qpos(x)qneg(x)) dvolume(x).
The set in this supremum ranges over exactly those absolute differences for measurable events B. The notation (P(B)).toReal means the real value of the extended nonnegative measure value P(B); the supremum is the real conditionally complete supremum. No separate event-distance estimate is assumed.

Then x ↦ √(qpos(x)qneg(x)) is integrable with respect to volume, and all of the following hold:
  0 ≤ a,
  a ≤ 1,
  δ ≤ √(1 − a²),
  a ≤ √(1 − (1/4) exp(−(10n)/√κ)),
  √(1 − (1/4) exp(−(10n)/√κ)) ≤ exp(−(1/8) exp(−(10n)/√κ)).
In these last expressions n is coerced to ℝ, and the exponent 2 in a² is the natural-number exponent 2. All displayed integrals of real-valued functions are real Bochner integrals, and integrability means genuine absolute Bochner integrability. Every unspecified Euclidean integral uses volume. Square roots are the nonnegative real square roots with the totalized real convention, and real division and inverse have their totalized conventions at zero.
scopes: All definitions are local to n and κ. μ is Haar on full O(n), while νpos and νneg separately use determinant +1 and −1 restrictions. qpos integrates p against νpos and qneg against νneg; Ppos and Pneg bind the same γ against their respective measures. The supremum defining δ uses measurable B in E and Ppos.real B=(Ppos B).toReal, Pneg.real B=(Pneg B).toReal. The integral defining a uses volume on E. The denominator (2π)^((n:ℝ)/2) uses Real.rpow with a real exponent; a² uses natural exponent 2. Every occurrence of 10n in the bounds uses the real coercion of n. Matrix inverse and real square root/division use the approved totalized conventions.
